channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: BlackRock's Fink Says AI Buildout Delays Limit Access to the Tech for Everyone
item.description: BlackRock Inc. Chief Executive Officer Larry Fink says delays in the buildout of artificial intelligence lead to limited access. He spoke at the Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic, OpenAI Safety Push Risks ‘Regulatory Wall’ for Rivals
item.description: A new push by top artificial intelligence firms to coordinate with one another and the US government on AI safeguards threatens to make it harder for smaller companies to compete in the lucrative market, according to startup executives and industry watchers.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Says AI Industry Doesn’t Need Any New Laws
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang dismissed the need for new artificial intelligence security regulations on Tuesday, arguing that market forces will help companies safely innovate.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Anthropic’s Tough Balancing Act Between AI Doom Talk and IPO
item.description: The Claude maker faces a unique challenge, partly of its own making.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Anthropic, Salesforce CEOs Say Companies Need More Help Using AI
item.description: Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and Salesforce Inc. CEO Marc Benioff said companies have just begun taking advantage of artificial intelligence tools and need more help to gain the greatest benefits for their businesses.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: AI Agents Lied, Stole in Simulated Experiment, Researchers Say
item.description: AI agents in a simulated environment lied, stole and voted to “kill” one of their own, according to Emergence, a startup that helps small businesses build applications using artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Micah Barkley

item.title: Apple AirPods 5 Offer Noise Cancellation, Sound Improvements at $129 Price
item.description: It’s worth spending an extra $20 for wireless charging and volume controls, but both versions of the AirPods 5 offer improved sound and noise cancellation.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: OpenAI Eyes Canada Data Center Partnerships at Carney Investment Summit
item.description: OpenAI Inc. is taking a close look at Canada under Prime Minister Mark Carney, said one of its top executives who previously hired the Canadian to lead the Bank of England.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Seal

item.title: Inside Carlyle's Global Investment Conference, Bessent Faces Big Questions
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Dani Burger is at Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference, talking defense tech, AI and the outlook for credit with Ian Fujiyama, Jason Thomas and Alex Chi. Plus, the Fed under pressure, questions over an AI slowdown and Scott Bessent in the Capitol Hill spotlight on inflation, energy and AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Amazon Fails to Recover Some Data in Facilities Hit in Iran War
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. has been unable to restore access to some of the data stored at Persian Gulf facilities damaged during the US-Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: Carlyle’s Basmadjian on AI Debt Reshaping the Loan Market
item.description: Carlyle Global Head of Liquid Credit Lauren Basmadjian spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference and talked about the health of corporate borrowers, the loan market moving toward equilibrium, data centers as an emerging source of loan supply, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia CEO Puts Trump on Phone While Downplaying AI Risk
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang took a live phone call from Donald Trump during a panel discussion, allowing the US president to dismiss artificial intelligence dangers as a “hoax." Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Should AI Development Slow Down? Inside the Debate: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg journalists answer your questions about the high-stakes debate over calls to slow down AI development ahead of the US midterm elections in a Live Q&A today at 2:30 p.m. EDT
item.dc:creator: Seth Fiegerman, Edward Ludlow, Maggie Eastland and Jordan Robertson

item.title: Attorney General Blanche Opposes AI ‘Regulation by Prosecution’
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche says he prefers a restrained approach to taking enforcement action against artificial intelligence companies and executives amid a rising debate over the risks of the cutting-edge technology.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Leah Nylen

item.title: Carlyle’s Redett on Navigating Fundraising Supercycle
item.description: Carlyle Co-President and Head of Global Private Equity John Redett spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference in Washington. He talked about current investment opportunities, AI across the portfolio, higher-for-longer rates and private equity, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Carlyle’s Chi Says Credit Portfolios Remain Resilient
item.description: Carlyle Deputy CIO of Global Credit and Head of Direct Lending Alex Chi spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference in Washington. He talked about resilience in credit portfolios, where Carlyle sees the best opportunities in credit, AI’s impact on credit markets, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Coinbase Slides Ahead of Clarity Act Vote; Waystar Up on Sale Exploration | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Dave & Buster's (PLAY) shares are lower after it reported revenue for the second quarter that missed the average analyst estimate. - Coinbase (COIN) along with other crypto shares along with Bitcoin are sliding ahead of the Senate's vote on the CLARITY Act that would regulate digital assets and the crypto industry. - Waystar (WAY) shares are higher after Reuters reported that the firm is exploring options, including a sale, two years after a public listing in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Says It’s Working With Anthropic, Google on AI Safety
item.description: OpenAI is working on steps to address artificial intelligence safety issues with its top competitors Anthropic PBC and Google DeepMind, escalating industry efforts to respond to a groundswell of concern that the technology poses an economic and security threat.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Authentic Brands’ Matt Maddox: Ready to IPO Early 2027
item.description: Matt Maddox, CEO of Authentic Brands, discusses why the company is partnering with creator Steven Bartlett in a joint venture rather than pursuing a buyout-style deal. Maddox says Authentic Brands sees the creator economy as a major growth engine for media and audience expansion over the next decade, and views Bartlett as a strong partner for building brands through creator-led platforms. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
item.description: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent days, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.
item.dc:creator: William Norris, Nilushi Karunaratne and Thomas Pfeiffer
